fields.meta_title: Employment Verification Letter Sample and Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: What an employment verification letter confirms, a short sample, and an app that drafts each letter from your HR records. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Employment Verification Letter Generator for HR
fields.hero_description: An employment verification letter confirms someone's job and dates of service. Describe how HR handles requests, and Emergent builds the request form and the letter behind it.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Verification Letter
fields.features_subheading: An employment verification letter template gives you the wording. Emergent adds the request form and HR sign-off that every letter passes through.
fields.feature_1:
One request form for every requester

Asks who wants the letter and where it should go, then collects the employee's signed consent on the same page. Lenders get their own questions, and landlords get a shorter set.
fields.feature_2:
Letters drafted from the HR record

Pulls the job title and start date straight from your employee table into the letter. Nobody retypes a hire date from memory or edits the copy someone saved two years ago.
fields.feature_3:
Salary only when the employee agrees

Adds base pay to a letter only when the employee has said yes on the request form. Every other letter confirms the job and its dates and leaves compensation out entirely.
fields.feature_4:
A signature before anything is sent

Sends each draft to the HR manager to read and sign on screen. Only then does the PDF go out on company letterhead, with a contact a lender can call to confirm what it says.
fields.feature_5:
A record of every letter you sent

Logs each request beside the letter it produced, with the signer and send date, in a database you own. When a lender calls back next spring, the exact letter is one search away.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full source

Publishes the request page on your own domain or inside the HR portal you already run. Developers get the complete source in GitHub for anything the original prompt left out.

fields.tab_content_1:
Lender forms answered from the payroll record

A lender's Form 1005 arrives as a PDF with the borrower's signed authorization. Emergent reads the fields it asks for and fills hire date, title and base pay from your HR table. Nothing goes back to the lender until someone in payroll approves the reply, and each reply is logged with the lender's name.
fields.tab_content_2:
A signed letter for the landlord, salary optional

Employees request a letter from a short form that asks who it is addressed to and whether salary should appear. Salary is added only when the employee ticks that box. The HR manager signs, and the landlord receives a PDF on company letterhead stating the job title and full-time status.
fields.tab_content_3:
Dates of service and the final title, nothing more

Anyone with an end date in the HR table gets a narrower letter: first day, last day and final job title. An HR generalist reviews each one before release. In Missouri, a former employee who asks in writing by certified mail can get a service letter within 45 days that also states why they left.
fields.tab_content_4:
No signed release, no answer

Screening firms use a verification page instead of calling HR. The firm names the candidate and uploads the signed release, and the app checks dates and title against the employee table. A request without a release goes back to the firm with a note, and nothing is confirmed until the release is on file.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Verification Letter
fields.howto_description: A sample employment verification letter shows the wording. These seven steps settle what HR confirms, who signs and where each letter goes.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Check who is asking and why
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put it on letterhead with a signer
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Pull every fact from the record
fields.howto_step_1_des: Confirm the request names the employee and says what the letter is for, such as a lease or a mortgage. Ask for the employee's written consent before you confirm anything, even a start date, and keep that consent with the request.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Most letters confirm full name, job title, start date and whether the person works full or part time. Leave salary off unless the employee asks for it. Opinions on performance and reasons for leaving stay out unless a state law requires them.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Print the verification of employment letter on company letterhead and address it to the requester by name. Close with an HR signature above a printed name, plus a direct phone number a landlord or lender can call to check it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Copy dates and pay from the HR system, never from the employee's resume or the request itself. When they disagree, the record wins. Tell the employee about the mismatch before the letter is sent.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Add a review step for exceptions
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send unusual letters to a second person before they go out, such as anything for a former employee or anything that discloses salary. Routine letters for current staff can go straight to the signer for a quick read and signature.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send it to the requester directly
fields.howto_step_6_des: Email the signed PDF to the address on the request, or upload it to the lender's portal. A letter that reaches the landlord from your HR inbox is harder to question than one the employee forwards from a personal account.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Keep a copy of each letter
fields.howto_step_7_des: Store every signed letter next to the request and the consent that came with it. If a lender calls months later to confirm employment again, HR can see exactly what was stated and who signed it without searching old email threads.

Fannie Mae Form 1005 is the Request for Verification of Employment lenders send to employers
